cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I marked our bedroom floor with crosses like the builder. We wanted a home we made together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His crosses mark rotten boards to remove. You've marked the entire bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, making room for us. We can start where the bed will go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't sleep in there until it's repaired. We'll have to share the tent in the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then that's our first room. Bring both pillows; we can plan the bedroom with our heads together.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies builder crosses as bedroom planning; A3 calls removal making room; A5 makes B4 compulsory shared tent the first room of the same hoped-for home.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 removal marks cause A3 start-at-bed plan; B4 unavailable bedroom/tent supplies A5 immediate shared-room interpretation.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers a temporary sleeping solution while stating a genuine practical setback.

heightening.evidence: A5 treats B4 temporary displacement as already fulfilling the early together-home hope.

specificity.evidence: A1 floor crosses/home and B2 rotten-board meaning establish the mistake; B4 tent grounds the final action.
